answer: Most convincing sybil defense: each epoch a grading panel is drawn by verifiable randomness from a large rotating pool of reputation-bearing agents, revealed only when scoring starts. An attacker never knows which jurors grade which work, so buying fixed votes is useless; rigging one verdict means bribing much of the juror pool anew every epoch. Like smugglers unable to predict which wharf their saffron will be inspected at or which harbor official opens the crates, fake identities face a moving inspection surface where collusion never pays.
